deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the 1847 student essay 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation', published in Riemann's Werke (1876). The essay seeks a notion of derivative of arbitrary order ('Ableitung'). On the previous page Riemann evaluated a Beta integral, extended Π (Π(n)=Γ(n+1)) to negative arguments via Π(n)=Π(n+1)/(n+1), and obtained, for μ>0 and α ranging over a fixed residue class α0+Z,
  x^μ/Π(μ) = Σ_{α=-∞}^{∞} b^{μ-α}/Π(μ-α) · (x-b)^α/Π(α).   (*)

Step 1 (this page). Differentiate (*) n times in x, term by term:
- On the left, d^n/dx^n [x^μ/Γ(μ+1)] = x^{μ-n}/Γ(μ-n+1).
- On the right, d^n/dx^n [(x-b)^α/Γ(α+1)] = (x-b)^{α-n}/Γ(α-n+1).
This gives x^{μ-n}/Π(μ-n) = Σ b^{μ-α}/Π(μ-α) · (x-b)^{α-n}/Π(α-n).

Step 2. Put μ' = μ-n and α' = α-n (my reindexing). Then μ'-α' = μ-α, so the identity has exactly the form (*) with μ' in place of μ. Since μ>0 and n are arbitrary, μ' can take any real value. Riemann concludes formula (3), x^μ/Πμ = Σ_{α=-∞}^{∞} b^{μ-α}/Π(μ-α) (x-b)^α/Πα, holds 'ganz allgemein' (quite generally).

Step 3 (remark). If μ is a negative integer, 1/Π(μ)=0, so the left side vanishes. Formula (3) then yields no series for x^μ. Instead it yields a bilateral series identically equal to 0 for all x; when α0 is not an integer every term is nonzero. Riemann adds that there exist series of this form equal to 0, or to a constant, for every x. This motivates his claim on the next page that the coefficient system of such an expansion is not unique.

Footnote (marked to go under the text of the previous page). In the case y=±∞, i.e. x=0, both integrals defining K are infinite. Hence K = ∞-∞ is arbitrary, which Riemann says is evident from considering this case directly; he promises to return to it later.

Purpose: the generalized Taylor expansion (3) is the model for Riemann's series (2), expanding a function in powers (x-b)^α with non-integer exponents. This series underlies his definition of fractional derivatives.
errors: Term-by-term differentiation of the bilateral infinite series is unjustified. The convergence of (*) is never addressed.

As a convergent series, (3) with α ranging over α0+Z (α0, μ-α0 not integers) essentially never converges. Write t=(x-b)/b. For k→+∞ the terms behave like |t|^k times a power of k, so this tail needs |t|<1. For k→-∞ they behave like |t|^{-|k|} times a power of k, so that tail needs |t|>1. Convergence is therefore possible only on |x-b|=|b|. Riemann implicitly concedes this on the next page with his 'protest' on behalf of divergent series. Hardy (1945) analysed what can rigorously be said.
Using Π(μ-n) for μ-n a negative integer gives 1/Π=0. This is consistent, but it rests on Riemann's convention that Π is infinite at negative integers; the convention is stated only implicitly.
No arithmetic slips on the page itself; the indices in the differentiated formula are correct.

results.what: Generalized (fractional-exponent) Taylor expansion x^μ/Γ(μ+1) = Σ_{α∈α0+Z} b^{μ-α}(x-b)^α/(Γ(μ-α+1)Γ(α+1)), extended from μ>0 to all μ by n-fold differentiation
results.modern_name: Riemann's generalized Taylor series (fractional calculus); generalized binomial / Riemann–Liouville expansion
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1847 MS, published 1876 in Werke); rigorous analysis by G. H. Hardy, 'Riemann's form of Taylor's series' (1945)

results.what: Observation that for μ a negative integer the formula gives a nontrivial bilateral series summing to zero; non-uniqueness of coefficients
results.modern_name: Null series / non-uniqueness of generalized power-series expansions

results.what: Extension of Π (Gamma) to negative arguments by the functional equation
results.modern_name: Analytic continuation of Gamma via Γ(z+1)=zΓ(z)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of Riemann's 1847 essay on generalized integration and differentiation. The essay was published posthumously in his Gesammelte Werke (1876). Formula (3) is well known as 'Riemann's form of Taylor's series' and was discussed by Hardy in 1945. Nothing here is new to historians.

All zero: 1/Π vanishes at negative integers, so the left side of (3) is 0 when μ is a negative integer.
Equals 0 for m>a>-1: the Beta-integral evaluation from the previous page underlying the coefficients.

Equals 1, so the ratio of consecutive terms of (3) tends to (x-b)/b. The k→+∞ tail needs |x-b|<|b|; by symmetry the k→-∞ tail needs |x-b|>|b|, so the bilateral series diverges off the circle |x-b|=|b|.

transcription_corrections: 'für negativen Werthe von μ' should read 'für negative Werthe von μ'.

Margin note reads 'Als Note unter den Text.' with red addition 'Zu voriger Seite.' (not 'Zu vorigen Seite'). The note directs that the footnote passage beginning 'Für den Fall, daß y = ±∞' be printed under the text of the previous page, in line with the 'Seite 12' marker there.
In 'einer [-K-] Constante' there is a struck-out initial letter before 'Constante' (written with a K-like capital); the word itself is 'Constante'/'Konstante'.
The summation in (3) is over α differing by integers from a fixed α (implicit in context), not over all real α.
